summary: Chelsea beat ten-man then nine-man Tottenham 4-1 at Tottenham's home ground, ending Spurs' unbeaten Premier League start. Nicolas Jackson scored a 75th-minute winner and two injury-time goals for his first hat-trick, after Cole Palmer's penalty had cancelled out Dejan Kulusevski's early opener. Cristian Romero and Destiny Udogie were sent off, and Spurs also lost Mickey van de Ven and James Maddison to injury. The note also covers Ange Postecoglou's reaction, his first home defeat as a manager in 52 matches, and the upcoming fixtures.
one_line: Chelsea beat nine-man Tottenham 4-1 as Nicolas Jackson scored a hat-trick, ending Spurs' unbeaten Premier League start and Postecoglou's home run.
key_facts: Tottenham suffered their first Premier League loss of the season, losing 4-1 at home to Chelsea (the article's opening line mistakenly says 2-1 before the late goals).
Dejan Kulusevski put Tottenham ahead in the sixth minute after a flicked pass from Pape Matar Sarr.
Cristian Romero was sent off after a lengthy VAR review for a high-footed challenge on Enzo Fernandez, and Chelsea were awarded a penalty.
Cole Palmer equalised from a 35th-minute penalty; Guglielmo Vicario got a touch but the ball deflected off the right post into the net.
Destiny Udogie was sent off in the 55th minute for a second bookable offence, leaving Spurs with nine men.

Nicolas Jackson scored the 75th-minute winner from a Raheem Sterling pass, then added goals in the 94th minute (from Connor Gallagher's pass) and the 97th minute (from Palmer's pass) for his first Premier League hat-trick.
Mickey van de Ven and James Maddison both went off injured at half-time, replaced by Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and Emerson Royal.
Ange Postecoglou's first home defeat as a manager ended a 52-match unbeaten home run that began in November 2020 at Yokohama F. Marinos and continued at Celtic and Tottenham.
Mauricio Pochettino returned to the ground where he managed Spurs from 2014-19; Chelsea's win was their fourth league win of the season and lifted them to tenth on goal difference.
Tottenham fell to second in the table before the match and sit second afterwards.
Postecoglou told BBC: 'There was a fair bit going on, a lot of VAR intervention' and said he was very proud of his players.
Sterling had a goal ruled out for handball, and Moises Caicedo had an equaliser disallowed for Jackson interfering with play.
Tottenham next visit Wolves on Saturday 11 November; Chelsea host Manchester City on Sunday 12 November at Stamford Bridge.
